findings.location: design section 3.2, sentence 'no other key's schema existence is revealed (INV-2)' and the Security assessment INV-2 line
findings.issue: Oracle analysis of the new both-lists-empty 422. Key names are no longer echoed, but the STATUS still differs: an assignee who submits a guessed key K outside the form with a schema-violating value gets 422 when K has a variable_schema that rejects it, and a normal completion (200) when K has no schema (omitted by validations_for, variable_schema.ex 407-436). So existence of a rejecting schema for a GUESSED name is still inferable from the status. Conclusions: (a) the both-empty body is indistinguishable by shape from any other refusal and carries no name, so the body itself leaks nothing; the leak is the 422-versus-accept status, which cannot be removed without dropping the whole-batch refusal (the design deliberately keeps it, rejecting silent dropping); (b) it is a confirm-a-guess channel, not an enumeration channel (no names returned), and a negative probe completes the task, so it is one-shot per task; (c) it is strictly narrower than today, where the same probe commits instance ERROR and answers 409 (design 3.1), a destructive and already-available oracle that this design removes the destructive half of; (d) variable-key names are definition data, not tenant business data. Hence not an INV-2 FAIL, but the sentence 'no other key's schema existence is revealed' overclaims.
findings.required_change: Reword the sentence in 3.2 and the INV-2 assessment line to: names of other keys are not revealed; a caller who guesses a key name can still observe from the 422-versus-accept status whether a rejecting schema exists for it, a residual accepted because it is no wider than today's behaviour (ERROR/409) and refusing it would require silently dropping values. Can be folded into the next doc touch; does not require a re-review round.
